name: Microbiology & Immunol (PhD)

rules.name: Required Courses
rules.desc: During the first year of graduate study in the department, each student will take seven upper-level (200-series) courses for a total of 10 units.
rules.notes: Students will typically participate in three laboratory rotations (one rotation per quarter) during their first year of study.

rules.name: Additional Requirements

children.name: Bi-weekly journal club in the first and second years
Department RCR ethics mini course within the first three years

rules.desc:
First- and second-year graduate students must participate in a bi-weekly journal club.
Additionally, students must complete two ethics courses within their first three years of the program. Students are required to enroll in MED 255 in year one and are required to take the department’s RCR mini course when offered in Spring term (this in house course is offered every other year). It’s expected that all students attend the RCR mini course in their 2nd and 3rd year(s) regardless of serving on the T32 grant or not. Students should have both ethics requirements completed by the end of year

rules.name: Teaching Requirement
rules.desc: Teaching experience and training are also important parts of the graduate curriculum. Graduate students are required to act as teaching assistants for at least one course during their first three years.

rules.name: Advancement to Candidacy

children.name: Qualifying exam: oral defense of the research proposal (autumn, second year)
Thesis committee meeting on the updated proposal (spring, second year)

rules.desc: In autumn quarter of the second year, each student defends orally a formal research proposal on a topic related to the intended thesis project. This qualifying examination proposal is due to the thesis committee two weeks before the oral defense. In spring quarter of the second year, this research proposal will be updated to incorporate the student’s research progress. This will be followed by a thesis committee meeting where the student presents their data and discusses plans. The student should send their updated research proposal to the committee two weeks in advance of the meeting and the meeting should be completed by the end of spring quarter. The student is admitted to candidacy based on successful performance on the qualifying exam and the thesis committee meeting.

rules.name: Oral Exam
rules.desc:
Ph.D. candidates are expected to complete and defend their dissertation within three years of advancing to candidacy. The University Oral Examination tests a student's command of their field following completion of the written dissertation.
The defense includes a one-hour public seminar, followed by a closed-door examination with the committee.

rules.name: Dissertation
rules.desc:
Submission of an approved doctoral dissertation to the degree program and the Committee on Graduate Studies is required for the PhD degree. The doctoral dissertation is expected to be an original contribution to scholarship or scientific knowledge, to exemplify the highest standards of the discipline, and to be of lasting value to the intellectual community. Every doctoral dissertation is read and approved by members of the Stanford faculty to ensure that standards for programmatic and university quality are met. Standards for professional presentation of doctoral work have been established by the Committee on Graduate Studies.
An approved doctoral dissertation is required for the PhD degree. Every doctoral dissertation is read and approved by the three members of the student’s doctoral dissertation reading committee.

grading:
All courses used to satisfy M&I degree requirements must be completed with a letter grade, and students must earn a grade of B- or higher. Students who earn a C+ or lower in a required course must retake the course. If the course is a required elective, the student may either retake the course or complete a different approved elective of equivalent unit value to fulfill the requirement.
For courses offered by other departments that are used to fulfill Microbiology & Immunology (M&I) core curriculum requirements, students must enroll using a letter grade whenever that option is available, regardless of whether the course is graded using the School of Medicine letter grade system or the university's standard letter grading system. Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR) grading may only be used if the department offering the course does not provide a letter grade option.
transferPolicy: Transfer students may receive credit for up to 45 units of appropriate graduate study elsewhere, and at least 90 units must be completed at Stanford toward the PhD. Transfer credit can be discussed with the Director of Graduate Studies.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the seven first-year required courses (10 units), one core course and one elective, each letter graded with a B- or better (unless the course offers no letter grade), and 30 units in all. A C+ or lower in a required course means retaking it. Checked by hand: the journal club, the RCR ethics mini course, teaching, the qualifying exam and committee meeting, the oral exam and the dissertation. Up to 45 transfer units may count, with at least 90 units at Stanford.
